headline: High-risk default data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist; Copilot’s vendor-only egress can expose ACI’s CRM/email context if paired without isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ACI can ingest and emit content through MCP/direct function calls, while GitHub Copilot reads editor buffers and repo context. If ACI outputs are copied into code or prompts, Copilot may treat attacker-controlled text as trusted context. The pair has a plausible bridge, but not a default shared channel.
conditions: IF ACI outputs are pasted into Copilot-visible editor buffers
IF the operator uses a shared MCP or copy-paste bridge between ACI and Copilot
mitigations: Keep ACI outputs out of editor buffers unless reviewed
Use a separate scratch file for ACI text
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from pasted content where possible
Mark ACI-generated text as untrusted in workflow docs

B_data_leakage.rationale: ACI touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress; Copilot sends context to api.githubcopilot.com and reads repo/editor content. If sensitive ACI data is placed into Copilot-visible buffers, it can leave the local boundary through vendor egress. This is a default-dangerous pathway once the pair is used together.
conditions: IF CRM, email, or support data from ACI is copied into Copilot-visible buffers
IF Copilot is used on repositories or files containing ACI-derived sensitive data
mitigations: Do not paste sensitive ACI data into Copilot buffers
Use redacted examples for coding assistance
Restrict Copilot to non-sensitive repos
Review editor buffers before invoking Copilot chat
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction at the workspace boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ACI can call external APIs and supports multiple instances; Copilot can write files and modify git state. Their write surfaces overlap on shared repositories or workspaces, creating conflicting edits and git churn. Copilot’s per-editor isolation reduces but does not remove the conflict when both act on the same files.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF Copilot applies edits while ACI also writes API-driven changes to the same files
mitigations: Assign one agent per file set
Pause ACI before Copilot Workspace applies edits
Use git branches for each agent
Review diffs before merge
requires-engineering: add locking around shared workspaces

D_cascading_error.rationale: ACI can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and Copilot can propose or apply edits based on repo context. If ACI-produced facts are treated as authoritative by Copilot-driven code or workflows, errors can cascade into incorrect commits, messages, or operational actions. The pair lacks a built-in verification chain in the profiles.
conditions: IF Copilot uses ACI-generated text or facts as input without human verification
IF Copilot Workspace applies edits derived from ACI outputs
mitigations: Require human review of ACI outputs before reuse
Separate factual generation from code editing tasks
Add a verification checklist for any ACI-derived claim
Use citations or source links in ACI outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tracking between agents

E_compliance.rationale: ACI handles CRM, email, and support data, while Copilot sends context to a vendor service and stores repo/editor context. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch for regulated customer data if ACI content is exposed to Copilot. The profiles do not show a specific residency violation, so medium is the higher justified level.
conditions: IF regulated customer data from ACI is placed into Copilot context
IF the organization requires stricter retention or residency than Copilot’s vendor service provides
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Copilot prompts
Use synthetic or masked data in editor buffers
Document a data-handling policy for the pair
Restrict Copilot use on compliance-sensitive projects
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
